verdict.rationale: GitLab documents built-in AI (GitLab Duo) that acts on tasks inside the product: agentic vulnerability resolution, analyzing failed dependency-bump pipelines to provide fixes, and homepage claims that agents turn issues into merge requests and review code. The detailed documentation covers only security-scoped workflows, and the broader delegation claim comes only from marketing copy. missing for 10: documentation of how a user hands an arbitrary task to the assistant (chat or issue assignment), evidence that general-purpose delegation goes beyond security remediation, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Teams orchestrate, agents execute, turning issues into merge requests, remediating vulnerabilities, and reviewing code, all inside the guardrails you set.
This agentic approach uses multi-shot reasoning to resolve vulnerabilities with minimal human intervention.
When a merge request that bumps a dependency has a failed pipeline, GitLab Duo can analyze the failure and provide fixes to resolve it.
For Ultimate tier customers with a GitLab Duo add-on, false positive detection runs automatically after each security scan and provides confidence scores with explanations for each assessment.
Every agent action shows up in the audit trail.
